we have defined and formally described a new category-based access control (ABAC) model that adds structure to ABACC, so that policies become more easily understood and maintained, review queries become easier to evaluate, and simpler systems such as role-based access control (RBAC) can be implemented as ABAC instances without additional costs.
we have proposed a category-based model for ABAC that makes it easier to understand, specify, and implement.
we propose a formal category-based model for attribute-based access control (ABAC) and that we prove that it is equivalent to the traditional model of ABAC.

the question: How can the benefits of ABAC be achieved with a model that is easier to design and maintain than the traditional ABAC model?

the following questions: 1. How do we model ABAC in the CBAC metamodel, so as to capture all its expressive power?

our proposed approach provides a more structured and efficient way to design and implement ABAC policies.
our proposed approach adds structure and simplicity to ABAC, without losing any of its expressivity and power.
the category-based model is a powerful tool to design ABAC systems that is more expressive than RBAC but easier to use.

our approach makes ABAC simpler, cheaper, and easier to use.

we propose an extension to the ABAC metamodel to support a more structured and manageable representation for ABAC policies, while still preserving all its expressiveness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ABAC can benefit from a more formal definition and that a category-based model of ABAC can be used as a basis for future work in the area.
CBAC is a powerful metamodel for ABAC that allows us to express ABAC in a more intuitive way, and to leverage the benefits of CBAC for ABAC.
CBAC can be applied to ABAC as well, and that the resulting model is more expressive than CBAC, and more flexible than ABAC.
